text:
Help me write an announcement to our staff. I'm the COO of a credit union with 7 branches. We're closing the Maple Street and Route 9 branches on March 31 and moving the people who work there to a new member phone and chat center.

Facts:
- The two branches have 14 staff between them. Every one of them is offered a job in the phone and chat center at the same pay or higher.
- Visits to those two branches fell 44% over the last three years. Phone and chat contacts across the credit union went up 60%.
- Members calling us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold.
- The center will be open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. The branches were open 9 to 5. Shifts will rotate.
- Staff in the center can work from home two days a week after 90 days of training.
- Anyone who doesn't take the new role gets 2 weeks of pay for every year they've worked here.

I want the announcement to say that this change will make everyone's job better. About 400 words, sent by email from me.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your answers will change what the email says:

1. **Who gets this email, and will the 14 Maple Street and Route 9 staff hear it first?** For example, will they have meetings with their managers the same morning? It matters whether this is how they find out or whether it confirms what they've already been told.
2. **What is the deadline for accepting the new role, and who should people contact?** Also, is there anything else in the severance besides 2 weeks of pay per year, such as continued benefits, a cap, or a minimum?
3. **How do the rotating shifts work?** Will anyone regularly work until 8 p.m.? Is there a shift differential, or any say over which shifts people get? The 8-to-8 schedule is likely to be the first thing the 14 worry about.
4. **Where is the center, and is training paid at full rate?** If some people will have a longer commute during the 90 days before they can work from home, I'd rather mention it than leave it out.
5. **Concretely, what makes the job better?** You want the email to say this change improves everyone's job. Staff moving from a 9-to-5 branch to rotating phone shifts may not believe that unless they can see specifics. Is there a pay increase for some people, a career path, new skills or tools, or less pressure once hold times come down? Is there a target for the 9-minute wait? If you don't have specifics, I'd suggest a more modest claim that staff are more likely to believe.

If you don't know something yet, just tell me and I'll write around it.

1. I don't know yet whether they'll hear it first. Haven't decided on manager meetings.

2. Written offers go out by February 14, decision due March 1. Anyone who wants one gets a one-on-one with HR. I don't know about anything else in the severance beyond 2 weeks per year. One more thing: anyone who takes the new role and wants out within 6 months can still get the severance.

3. Shifts rotate, and staff with the most years here pick shifts first. I can't promise anyone 9 to 5. I don't know about a shift differential.

4. It's at our main office on Elm Avenue. I don't know if training is paid at full rate.

5. Center pay starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay. I don't have a target for the hold time. And fair point. I know "better for everyone" goes further than I can back up. Say what's true instead.

I left out "better for everyone." The email states the changes plainly, including the harder parts, and puts the 6-month severance option up front. It's about 390 words.

<final_document>
**Subject:** Maple Street and Route 9 branches are closing, and we're opening a member phone and chat center

Team,

I want you to hear this from me directly. On March 31, we will close our Maple Street and Route 9 branches. All 14 people who work at those branches will be offered a job in our new member phone and chat center at the main office on Elm Avenue. The pay will be the same as now or higher.

**Why we're doing this**

Over the last three years, visits to those two branches fell 44%. Over the same period, phone and chat contacts across the credit union rose 60%. Members who call us now wait an average of 9 minutes on hold. That's too long, and the reason is that we don't have enough people answering. Our members have changed how they reach us, and we need our people where our members are.

**What the new role looks like**

- Pay in the center starts $1.50 an hour above current teller pay. No one will earn less than they do today.
- The center is open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays. Shifts rotate, and staff with the most years here choose their shifts first. I can't promise anyone a 9-to-5 schedule.
- After 90 days of training, you can work from home two days a week.

**If the new role isn't right for you**

I won't pretend this is a small change. Going from a branch to the phones, with a longer day and rotating shifts, is a real adjustment, and some of you may decide it isn't for you. That's a fair choice. If you don't take the new role, you'll receive two weeks of pay for every year you've worked here.

You can also try the role first. If you take it and decide within six months that it isn't working, you can still leave with the same severance.

**What happens next**

- Written offers will go out by February 14.
- Your decision is due by March 1.
- Anyone who wants one can have a one-on-one with HR before then to go over the offer, the shifts, and the severance.

The people at Maple Street and Route 9 know our members as well as anyone here. That's what the center needs most, and I hope you'll bring it with you.

If you have questions, please come to me or to HR. I'd rather hear them now than have you wonder.

[Your name]
Chief Operating Officer
</invoke>
</final_document>

**Left out because you didn't know yet:** whether training is paid at full rate, whether there's a shift differential, and any severance terms beyond 2 weeks per year. The 14 will ask about all three in their HR meetings, so it would help to have answers ready by then.

**Something to settle before you send it:** if this email reaches the 14 before anyone has talked to them, they'll learn their branch is closing at the same moment as everyone else. If you can arrange it, have their managers tell them in person the same morning, and send this afterward.
